summary: The candidate passes. It is a docs-only change that addresses each of the prior attempt's findings. The new note checks the premise first: it cites the code (`landing_end` and `landing_record_time` in throughput.rs, which take the newest landing record) and section 6.1 of agent-and-build-slots.md. It concludes that the 1842.1-minute landing stage is mostly repeated listings of the same commit, not real waiting. It states the saving as minutes from verifier pass to first landing record (an estimate of 0 to about 5 minutes) and does not claim the 1830.0 minutes. I checked its numbers against the evidence snapshot: `status --snapshot` printed 1903.5 and 1842.1, and the job string appears in 60 of 215 landing files, with the first and newest files as named. These results are about the snapshot, not the live records. All function and line references in the Existing code table match the source. The note covers alternatives (including measuring from the first record, kept as a companion), failure cases, a scoring rule that reports both stages, and the citation duty. per-job-landing-branches.md now points to the new note. CHANGELOG.md gains an entry and docs/decisions.md gains decision D167. Only the 4 listed files change, and Athena's CI record shows fmt, clippy and tests passing. There is one minor problem: a leftover sentence in the older note's section 10 still reads as if the 1530.0-minute prediction will be scored. There are also two small wording nits in the new note's section 1.
